# F-### — Feature Name

> LLM instructions: Replace all placeholders before saving a real feature file. Keep this document functional and implementation-independent. Do not include architecture, frameworks, APIs, database design, component design, or implementation tasks unless they are explicitly approved product constraints.

## Purpose

Describe the user or product value this feature provides.

Keep this concise. State why the feature exists and the outcome it enables.

## Functional Description

Describe how the feature behaves from the product perspective.

Include:
- Who uses or consumes the feature when relevant.
- The primary user flow or functional behavior.
- Important states and outcomes.
- Functional boundaries that materially affect how the feature is understood.

Do not describe how the feature will be implemented.

## Functional Requirements

List the observable behaviors or outcomes the feature must provide.

Requirements should:
- Be clear enough for the Tech Lead to design a solution without inventing product behavior.
- Describe what must happen, not how it is implemented.
- Be individually understandable and testable at the product level.
- Avoid unnecessary detail that does not materially affect the feature.

Use concise bullets.

## Out of Scope

List functionality explicitly excluded from this feature when doing so prevents ambiguity or scope growth.

Do not invent exclusions that have not been agreed with the Product Manager.

If no explicit exclusions are needed, state:

None defined.

## Open Questions

List only unresolved functional questions that do not prevent the feature from being documented.

Questions that materially block a correct technical design should be resolved with the user before the feature is handed to the Tech Lead.

Remove questions when resolved and update the relevant section with the agreed behavior.

If there are no open questions, state:

None.
